_what: The objects the architect draws, built and completed by the electrical sheets (crossdisc.rs, Q6612): every electrical object the architect draws (a light on a reflected ceiling plan, a receptacle or a data outlet on a floor plan, a fan) is an object of the building; it must be completed the way an installer completes it (`requires`), and its completing object is the electrical sheets' object of its kind by it in its room. What no electrical sheet completes is the finding. Each kind is a row of `kinds`: how the architect's legend names it, which engineer's devices are it, how near its electrical copy must be, what it needs, what the build makes of it when no electrical sheet completes it.
_basis: The documents' own order and the codes: the architectural reflected ceiling plans, floor plans and interior elevations locate what the owner sees; the electrical plans give each one its type, circuit and control (NEC 210.11: every outlet on a branch circuit; NEC 210.70 and the energy code's lighting controls). An object no electrical sheet completes is one the field finds on site: the electrician builds what the architect shows and asks for its type and circuit.
_architect_disciplines: The sheet disciplines whose drawings are the architect's (architecture, interiors).
_architect_sheet_kinds: The architect's sheets read for objects: reflected ceiling plans, floor plans, enlarged plans (each placed on its level's plan).
_legend_title_words: A short heading holding one of these words heads a legend: the rows under it are its drawing beside its words.
_legend_title_max_words: A heading of more words is a note that mentions a legend, not one.
_legend_rows_h: A legend's rows reach at most this many row heights under its heading.
_legend_gap_h: A gap of more than this many row heights between two rows ends the legend (rows are spaced by their drawings: a ceiling tile's square, a fixture's bar); so does a heading taller than its rows under it.
_legend_row_max_words: A legend row names its symbol in a few words; a longer line under a legend's heading is a note, no row.
_legend_drawing_h: A row's drawing lies at most this many row heights left of its words.

kinds.name: lights
kinds._reach_ft: The electrical sheets' light this near the architect's in its room is that light (sheet registration and the electrical plan's schematic placing).
kinds._cluster_ft: Lights no electrical sheet completes, this near each other in one room, are one finding (an alcove's lights).

build.proposed_control: a single-pole switch at the room's door (NEC 210.70: a lighting outlet controlled by a switch at the entrance)
build.proposed_circuit: the nearest lighting circuit of the level the electrical plans give

kinds._requires: the luminaire schedule (type); NEC 210.11 (every outlet on a branch circuit); NEC 210.70 and the energy code's lighting controls (control)

kinds.name: exit signs
kinds._requires: IBC 1013 / NFPA 101 7.10 (an illuminated exit sign on its emergency source); NEC 700

kinds.name: receptacles
kinds._requires: NEC 210.11 (every outlet on a branch circuit)

kinds.name: data and telephone outlets
kinds._requires: the telecommunications drawings (a cable and pathway to its room)

kinds.name: exhaust and ceiling fans
kinds._requires: NEC 422 / 430 (a fan's branch circuit and disconnect)

kinds.name: powered door hardware (operators, card readers, electric strikes)
illuminated signs
kinds._requires: NEC 600.5 (a sign outlet on its own branch circuit)

rooms._reach_ft: An object this near a room (just outside its traced outline: a wall's thickness) is that room's; one outside every traced room is completed by one in a room only this near.

_max_findings: Open groups filed per run at most (one per room and kind); the rest are counted in the report.
_max_sketches: Marked-up plan crops made per run at most.
